# regeneration mode (the test's doc says how); classify each `unclassified` line by
# hand (known-old-bug, correction, spec-disagreement) with a note, or fix the
# regression. Columns:
# program <TAB> key <TAB> kind <TAB> class <TAB> old <TAB> new <TAB> note
# A field writes `\` as `\\`, a tab as `\t`, a newline as `\n`, a carriage return
# as `\r`; an old or new of `-` is no row, and a field that is `-` itself is `\-`.
crates/hale-types/tests/api_serve_check.rs#dc6ea11b	musl Linux TargetSpec::has_async_io placement `web`@1760	disagreement	correction	lower	placement entry `web`: `async_io` pools aren't supported on musl Linux yet — use a cooperative pool (drop `where async_io`), or build for glibc Linux or macOS. (The backend is epoll or kqueue over ucontext coroutines; this target's libc has no ucontext.)	an exposure's row places its listener (GH #1565): the expansion moves the written row to the listener param it adds to main, so the legacy table reads no async_io row under `web` and lowers it; the cell judges the row as written, which puts the listener on an async_io pool this target has no backend for
crates/hale-types/tests/api_serve_check.rs#dc6ea11b	wasm32 TargetSpec::has_async_io placement `web`@1760	disagreement	correction	lower	placement entry `web`: `async_io` pools aren't supported on wasm32 — use a cooperative pool on `main` (drop `where async_io` and the pool). (the runtime's LOTUS_HAVE_ASYNC_IO is 1 over epoll and eventfd imports the loader stubs with `() => 0`, and the pool's workers are threads the module does not have.)	an exposure's row places its listener (GH #1565): the expansion moves the written row to the listener param it adds to main, so the legacy table reads no async_io row under `web` and lowers it; the cell judges the row as written, which puts the listener on an async_io pool this target has no backend for
